title: Pin the operational interpretation engine for historical replay
author: Codex AI engineering review
currentBehavior: Model release 1.0.0 pins philosophical data but has no executable-source archive. Changes to route, response, interpretation, or affinity code can therefore alter replay without changing that manifest. A conditional question skipped by its branch previously counted as assigned evidence content.
proposedBehavior: Archive the nine current route, response, interpretation, localization, and affinity modules with exact hashes. The current engine excludes a branch-skipped conditional item from available route evidence and rejects impossible presentation records. Pin that archive in a new model release while retaining release 1.0.0 unchanged.
rationale: A saved result needs the behavior that interpreted its exact raw responses, not only the JSON definitions. A question never shown because its prerequisite failed cannot furnish an available direct evidence unit.

philosophicalBasis.proposition: A respondent-facing philosophical conclusion requires administered evidence that bears on its exact target.
neighboringViews: A question assigned to a route but branch-skipped is not an answered indicator.
An administered but unanswered question differs from an unassigned question.
nonEntailments: The respondent rejects the target proposition when a conditional question is skipped.
The archived authored rules are empirically validated.
philosophicalBasis.existingGap: The initial operational release does not pin executable interpretation code and a conditional route item could be counted as available despite never being shown.
philosophicalBasis.scholarlyDisagreement: No philosophical doctrine or source interpretation changes in this archive. The change concerns the provenance and availability of respondent evidence.

sourceClaims.claim: The project-specific evidence contract requires route and response provenance; this source is contextual and does not validate any philosophical inference or item.

alternatives: Rely on Git history for replay; rejected because an administration must name an immutable production configuration directly.
Edit model release 1.0.0 in place; rejected because historical manifest bytes must remain unchanged.
respondentImpact: A branch-skipped conditional discriminator cannot make a short route appear to have enough content. No raw answer is changed, and no philosophical position is inferred from the skip.
historicalCompatibility: Keep model release 1.0.0 and all of its component bytes unchanged. It predates engine-source pinning, so its exact historical executable behavior cannot be proven from that manifest alone. New administrations pin the archived engine through model release 1.1.0.

approvals.note: Checked the inference boundary: a branch skip is missing content, not opposition to the target or assent to a neighboring view.
Reviewed exact source paths, immutable archive hashes, and branch-skip regression cases; focused tests passed.

release.migration: No raw-response migration. Preserve the 1.0.0 manifest and activate the archive only through a new explicit model release.
